theory.intro: Use sine, cosine and tangent to build their reciprocal graphs.
facts: $\operatorname{cosec}x=1/\sin x$, $\sec x=1/\cos x$, $\cot x=\cos x/\sin x$.
Zeros of sine give cosecant and cotangent asymptotes; zeros of cosine give secant asymptotes.
Secant and cosecant have range $(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$ and period $2\pi$ ($360^{\circ}$).
Cotangent has range $\mathbb R$ and period $\pi$ ($180^{\circ}$). Its zeros occur at $\pi/2+k\pi$.
Secant is even. Cosecant and cotangent are odd.

foundation.solution_text:
The asymptotes are zeros of cosine.
$\sec x$

The asymptotes are zeros of sine.
$\operatorname{cosec}x$

The branches include $y=\pm1$ but no ordinate between them.
$(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$

foundation.question_text: State the period and symmetry of $\cot x$ using degrees.
foundation.solution_text:
Cotangent is odd and repeats after a half-turn.
$180^{\circ};\ \text{odd}$

development.solution_text:

Each branch covers all real ordinates.
$\mathbb{R}$
